title: Volume of a singleton in a finite type
statement: Let $k \ge 1$ be a natural number and let $a$ be an element of the finite type $\mathrm{Fin}\,k = \{0, 1, \dots, k-1\}$, equipped with its canonical (uniform) volume measure. Then the measure of the singleton $\{a\}$ equals $1/k$, as an element of the extended nonnegative reals $[0, \infty]$.
hypotheses_covered: k is a natural number with k ≥ 1 (NeZero k)
a is an element of Fin k
replaced:
For $k \ge 1$ and any $a : \mathrm{Fin}\,k$, the uniform measure of the singleton
$\{a\} \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,k$ equals $1/k$ as an extended non-negative real:
$\mu(\{a\}) = 1/k \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^\infty$.
